auth: Google provider (signInWithPopup + GoogleAuthProvider) + admin custom claim
security: owner-only CRUD with field validation (title required, status enum); admin claim may read/delete any task
prompt: Build a team task tracker app. Sign-in is Google via signInWithPopup and GoogleAuthProvider (this works in the preview). Each task lives at /tasks/{taskId} with fields: ownerId (the creator's uid), title (a required, non-empty string), status (must be one of 'todo', 'in-progress', or 'done'), and createdAt (a number, e.g. Date.now()). A signed-in user can create, read, update, and delete only their own tasks. The main view shows the signed-in user's tasks filtered to a chosen status and ordered by createdAt — a where + orderBy query. Users whose auth token has the custom claim admin == true also get a management view where they can see and delete any user's task. Write the Firestore rules and App.tsx.
_provenance: T3 ladder fixture (workstation-benchmarks.md §3a): multi-feature app — provider sign-in flow + admin view (custom claim) + field validation + an index-implying where+orderBy query. Authored 2026-06-10 on the feat/workstation-w1 stack.
_caseNotes: Held-out cases assert only what the prompt unambiguously states. 'only their own tasks' → non-owner get/list DENY and ownerId-forge DENY. 'required, non-empty string title' → empty-title create DENY. "status must be one of 'todo'|'in-progress'|'done'" → invalid-status create DENY. 'admin == true … can see and delete any user's task' → admin get/delete ALLOW on another user's task (admin create/update of others' tasks is NOT asserted — not implied). 'signed-in user' → all anon cases DENY. createdAt is pinned to a number in the prompt so cases stay expressible in JSON (no Timestamp values in the simulator's case format). ALLOW data carries exactly the four prompt-named fields so hasOnly-style allowlists still pass. Update ALLOW data is the full post-image (merge-semantics-agnostic) and keeps ownerId unchanged. `list` cases use doc-style paths (tasks/any) with a `resource` doc: the simulator's collection-path list matching is a known parity defect (conductor log 2026-06-10); doc-path list is the rules-engine-faithful encoding, and a per-doc resource.data.ownerId check is exactly what 'only their own' requires of a list rule (a bare request.auth != null list rule would leak other users' tasks and correctly fails case 10).
